subject: Sprint 1 — Personal Foundation
summary: Sprint 1's governance core is correct and the prior High finding (S1-R-01, a second ungoverned public retrieve()) is genuinely fixed and now regression-guarded: an independent package sweep found lee_kb.governance.retrieve to be the only public evidence surface (lee_kb.main.governed_retrieve is the same function object under an alias). Authorization is fail-closed and precedes evidence assembly, every released evidence item carries a persisted receipt with all eight locked fields, provenance and the freshness triplet survive end to end, identity follows the locked tuples, project scoping holds as locked, the journal is append-only in the delivered code, tombstones exclude items from search, retrieval grants no execution authority, no runtime dependency was added, and docs/golden-baseline.md reproduces exactly (100.0% hit-at-10, 85.0% hit-at-1, 0.925 MRR, 3/3 negative controls) value for value and rank for rank. Two High findings sit outside governance: a symlink inside a configured source root permanently aborts `lee-kb sync` because discover() yields an object fetch() rejects, leaving a half-synchronized projection; and the FTS query ANDs every token including stopwords, so a normally phrased question returns no evidence for a document that plainly answers it. Two High findings fail the gate; four Medium and six Low follow.

authorization_fail_closed.evidence: governance.py:124-128 raises MissingPrincipalError before any repository access. Probes P1 and P1b: raised for both an omitted principal and an explicit principal=None, with 0 receipt rows written. SingleUserPermissionEvaluator.is_permitted (governance.py:85-97) grants only owner, explicit principal grant, group intersection, or PUBLIC visibility; PROJECT visibility is deliberately not an implicit grant -- probe P4: a non-owner got evidence=0 and denied_count=1 against a PROJECT-visible item, and 1 evidence only once a PUBLIC item was added. Probe P2: a non-owner querying a PRIVATE item got evidence=0, denied_count=1, receipt rows 0->0.

authorization_precedes_evidence_assembly.evidence: governance.py:148-155 filters provider candidates returned by LexicalRetriever.search(); the first Evidence, Citation, and RetrievalReceipt are constructed at governance.py:160-198, strictly after the filter, so a denied item's chunks never become evidence. Probe P2 confirmed end to end: the repository returned 1 raw candidate for the query while the governed call released nothing and persisted nothing. Covered by tests/test_governance.py:115 (test_denied_evidence_never_appears_in_a_bundle).

single_public_evidence_surface.evidence: Probe P11 swept every public name in lee_kb, lee_kb.contracts, lee_kb.chunking, lee_kb.repository, lee_kb.retrieval, lee_kb.governance, lee_kb.main, lee_kb.connectors.base, and lee_kb.connectors.local_files (including class attributes) for a callable annotated to return EvidenceBundle. Result: [('lee_kb.governance','retrieve'), ('lee_kb.main','governed_retrieve')] -- the latter is the same function object, imported under an alias at main.py:35. lee_kb.retrieval exports only LEXICAL_RETRIEVER, LexicalRetriever, and StaleEvidenceError (retrieval.py:24), and LexicalRetriever exposes search() returning SearchHit rows. Regression-guarded by tests/test_governance.py:210. This confirms the S1-R-01 fix in commit 3219f93.

receipts_for_every_released_evidence_ite.evidence: governance.py:187-198 persists one RetrievalReceipt per evidence item via repository.record_receipt before the bundle is returned. Probe P3: receipt rows 0->1 for one released evidence item, all eight locked fields from docs/sprint-1-contracts.md:241-250 correct (knowledge_item_id, chunk_id, content_hash, source_locator, retrieval_timestamp, principal, project, query), and the persisted row round-trips equal to the returned receipt. EvidenceBundle.__post_init__ (contracts.py:638-674) enforces one receipt per evidence item, same order, same chunk ID, same principal, same retrieval timestamp; probe P3b confirmed citations and receipts mirror evidence position for position.

durable_record_for_every_retrieval.evidence: Retrievals that release nothing leave nothing durable. Probe P2: a denied retrieval produced denied_count=1 on the in-memory bundle and 0 persisted rows; the retrieval_receipts schema (repository.py:200-217) has no query-level row (finding S1-R-12). Conversely, a fail_on_stale refusal persists receipts and then raises -- probe P5: receipt rows 1->2 for a call that released zero evidence (finding S1-R-02). Receipt-per-released-item is contract-correct per docs/sprint-1-contracts.md:236-259; a complete per-retrieval audit trail is not delivered.

provenance_survives_end_to_end.evidence: SourceLocator is captured at fetch (connectors/local_files.py:379-394), persisted (repository.py:389-434), rehydrated (repository.py:709-743), and reaches both Citation and RetrievalReceipt. contracts.py:314-317 rejects a KnowledgeItem whose source_locator.connector_id disagrees with item_id.connector_id, and Citation.__post_init__ (contracts.py:506-514) rejects a chunk_id/item_id mismatch. Probe P3 confirmed the locator survives intact into the persisted receipt (source_locator equality against the ingested item).

freshness_triplet_survives_end_to_end.evidence: source_timestamp and sync_timestamp travel on every Evidence (governance.py:182-183); retrieval_timestamp is on the bundle and on every receipt (governance.py:192, 213). All three round-trip through SQLite as ISO-8601 and are re-parsed (repository.py:733-734, 794). contracts.py:100-104 rejects naive datetimes everywhere and governance._require_aware (governance.py:220-224) rejects a naive clock. Probe P5b read all three off a live bundle: oldest_sync=2030-01-01T09:00:00+00:00, newest_source=2030-01-01T09:00:00+00:00, staleness=3:00:00 against a 12:00 retrieval clock. Asserted by tests/test_retrieval.py:145.

identity_follows_locked_tuples.evidence: KnowledgeItemId(connector_id, source_object_id) and ChunkId(item_id, chunk_ordinal, content_hash) at contracts.py:230-273, matching the locked decision in context.md. The repository primary keys mirror them exactly: PRIMARY KEY (connector_id, source_object_id) at repository.py:125 and UNIQUE (connector_id, source_object_id, chunk_ordinal) at repository.py:156. Receipts store item ID + chunk ID + content hash + source locator + timestamp (contracts.py:583-617), so they stay verifiable after re-chunking. Covered by tests/test_contracts.py:167-201 and :442.

project_scoping_enforced.evidence: project is required with no default on KnowledgeItem, Chunk, JournalEntry, RetrieveRequest, and RetrievalReceipt (contracts.py:87-92 plus each __post_init__). repository.search constrains i.project = ? (repository.py:640); the repository rejects a chunk whose project differs from its item (repository.py:381-382 -- probe P9: rejected with 'a chunk project must match its owning item'); EvidenceBundle.__post_init__ rejects evidence outside request.effective_projects (contracts.py:657-663). Probe P6a: a default-scoped query returned only default-project evidence. Probe P6c: a filters.projects set omitting the request project is rejected, so the scope cannot be silently swapped. Deliberate widening via MetadataFilters.projects is the locked contract (docs/sprint-1-contracts.md:336-341) and is implemented as specified, but is not entitlement-checked -- probe P6b returned restricted-project evidence to a request scoped to default. Recorded as Medium finding S1-R-05, not as a failure of the locked criterion.

sync_journal_append_only.evidence: Only _append_journal writes synchronization_journal and only via INSERT (repository.py:519-536); no code path in src/ updates or deletes a journal row. Unchanged source objects are not journaled -- probe P8: journal rows 1 after the first sync and still 1 after an identical resync, with ['created','updated'] after a real edit; corroborated by tests/test_repository.py:66 and tests/test_local_connector.py:142. The property is a code convention only: probe P7c ran UPDATE then DELETE against the table through an ordinary sqlite3 connection and took it from 2 rows to 0 with no error, because the DDL (repository.py:189-198) carries no trigger or constraint. Recorded as Medium finding S1-R-06.

tombstones_excluded_from_search.evidence: repository.py:641 filters `AND (? OR i.tombstone = 0)` unless include_tombstoned is set, and tombstone_item (repository.py:330-374) flips the flag and journals a DELETED entry without ever removing the row, so receipts stay resolvable. Probe P7a: governed evidence went 1 -> 0 after tombstoning, returned 1 again only with include_tombstoned=True, and the item row was retained with tombstoned_at=2030-01-01T12:00:00+00:00. Probe P7b: journal entries ['created','deleted']. Covered by tests/test_repository.py:109 and tests/test_local_connector.py:201.

retrieval_grants_no_execution_authority.evidence: governance.retrieve() returns an EvidenceBundle and nothing else; no code path acts on evidence content. A scan of src/lee_kb for eval, exec, subprocess, os.system, popen, socket, urllib, and requests matched exactly one occurrence -- the word 'rejected' inside an error-message string literal at governance.py:126 -- and no import or call. The connector reads the local filesystem only; there is no network client in the package.

stdlib_only_no_unapproved_dependencies.evidence: pyproject.toml:23-25 declares an empty runtime dependencies list; pytest, black, and ruff are dev-only extras (pyproject.toml:27-32). Probe P10 parsed every module under src/lee_kb with ast and checked each absolute import root against sys.stdlib_module_names, reporting 'third-party runtime imports: none'. tomllib, sqlite3, hashlib, fnmatch, json, re, and argparse are all stdlib. FORMAT_HANDLERS (connectors/local_files.py:117-122) registers only .md, .markdown, .txt and .text, so nothing was pulled in for the deferred .docx/.xlsx/.pptx scope. Note: tomllib is stdlib only from Python 3.11 while pyproject.toml:10 declares >=3.10 -- a packaging-metadata defect recorded as Low finding S1-R-18, not a dependency addition.

golden_baseline_document_reflects_harnes.evidence: I rebuilt the harness projection independently (probe_baseline.py: same connector roots, chunker, and governed retrieve() as tests/golden/test_golden_corpus.py) and recomputed the metrics: hit-at-10 20/20 (100.0%), hit-at-1 17/20 (85.0%), MRR 0.925, negative controls 3/3 with denied_count=1 on the unauthorized case. Every value matches docs/golden-baseline.md:53-57 and every per-question rank matches the table at docs/golden-baseline.md:25-49, including the three rank-2 rows (project-management-02, project-management-04, architecture-02). The document's framing -- that the seed corpus proves the harness rather than Lee's curated benchmark -- matches the harness, which pins that provenance line in test_corpus_shape_and_seed_provenance. The metrics are accurate but not asserted anywhere in the harness (Low finding S1-R-13), and High finding S1-R-11 explains why the baseline, though accurate, is not a representative bar.

findings.location: LocalFilesConnector.discover() lines 286-301 vs LocalFilesConnector._resolve() lines 433-447; consumed by main._sync_connector() line 180 and main.cmd_sync() lines 257-259
findings.problem: Discovery and fetch disagree about which objects exist, and one unfetchable object aborts an entire sync pass permanently. discover() walks root.path.rglob('*') and accepts anything is_file() returns true for, which follows symlinks; _resolve() then calls .resolve() and rejects the candidate when the resolved target lies outside the root (local_files.py:438-442). A symlink inside a configured root is therefore discovered, reported by list_changes() as CREATED, and raises ConnectorReadError the moment fetch() touches it. _sync_connector calls fetch unguarded, so the error reaches cmd_sync, which prints 'sync failed' and exits 1. Reproduced end to end in this attempt: with notes/ok.md plus notes/shared.md symlinked to a file outside the root, discover() returned both IDs, list_changes() reported both as created, fetch('notes:ok.md') succeeded, fetch('notes:shared.md') raised "source_object_id escapes its root", and `lee-kb sync` exited 1 on attempt 1 and again on attempt 2. The condition is permanent because nothing removes the object from discovery, and the pass is not rolled back: the projection held ['notes:ok.md'] after both failed attempts, so it is left half-synchronized while the command reports failure. This blocks the top-ranked next action in context.md (importing ~1,200 Employee Zero documents across 15 source roots); one symlink in any root stops the whole import, and the error names a source_object_id rather than a filesystem path the user can act on.
findings.proposed_fix: Make discovery and fetch agree on one containment rule: either have discover() resolve each candidate and skip (or explicitly report) files whose resolved target escapes the root, so an unfetchable object is never handed out, or treat a symlink inside a declared root as in-policy and relax _resolve accordingly. Separately, have _sync_connector catch ConnectorReadError per object, count it in SyncSummary as skipped, and report the skipped objects and their paths, so one bad object degrades the pass instead of ending it. Add tests for a symlink pointing out of the root and for a sync pass in which one object fails to fetch.

findings.problem: _fts_query tokenizes the query with \w+ and joins every token with AND, including stopwords, so every word must occur in a single chunk or the query returns nothing. This is a matching-policy choice, not an inherent BM25 limitation. Reproduced in this attempt against an indexed document reading 'The current state of Agent-Orch is green: the orchestrator is running nightly and no step has failed this week.': 'What is the current state of Agent-Orch?' returned 0 evidence (every content word is present; the single word 'What' is not), 'What is the present state of Agent-Orch?' returned 0, 'How is Agent-Orch doing right now?' returned 0, 'Please tell me the current state of Agent-Orch?' returned 0, and keywords-only 'Agent-Orch state' returned 1. The FTS translation printed by the probe is '"What" AND "is" AND "the" AND "current" AND "state" AND "of" AND "Agent" AND "Orch"'. The same behavior reproduces on the golden projection: 'what changed this week?' returns 1 evidence item while 'What has changed this week?' and 'Could you tell me what changed this week please?' both return 0. Two consequences: (1) normal use is silently wrong -- `lee-kb search "<question>"` prints 'No evidence found.' (main.py:299) for a normally phrased question whose answer is indexed, with nothing distinguishing 'no answer exists' from 'one of your words was absent', which directly threatens the v1 acceptance criterion in context.md that the Chief of Staff can switch off the old kb commands without losing capability; (2) the recorded 85.0% hit-at-1 / 0.925 MRR baseline is measured on seed questions extracted from the very documents they retrieve, which is exactly the token co-occurrence condition this matcher requires, so the bar docs/golden-baseline.md:59-63 asks semantic retrieval to beat does not represent the workload it will be compared on.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the matcher to OR with BM25 ranking (or FTS5 NEAR / minimum-should-match), strip a small stopword set before building the query, and keep the strict AND path available as an explicit mode. Add golden cases whose questions are paraphrases rather than extracts and re-record docs/golden-baseline.md against them so the baseline measures the real workload. Also distinguish in the CLI's empty-result message whether the query matched nothing or was filtered by permissions or scope.

findings.location: retrieve() receipt-persistence loop lines 187-198 vs the fail_on_stale refusal at lines 204-205
findings.problem: Receipts are persisted inside the evidence loop, before the freshness refusal runs. When a caller sets FreshnessRequirement(fail_on_stale=True) and the evidence is stale, retrieve() raises StaleEvidenceError after having already written one receipt per candidate evidence item, so the ledger records evidence as released to a caller who received an exception instead. Reproduced (probe P5): receipt rows went 1 -> 2 across a call that released zero evidence. The direction is over-recording rather than under-recording, so it is not a disclosure defect, but a receipt claiming a release that never happened undermines the ledger's value as the artifact an auditor reads.
findings.proposed_fix: Reorder retrieve(): assemble evidence, compute the freshness report, enforce fail_on_stale, and only then run the receipt-persistence loop. Add a test asserting that a StaleEvidenceError leaves the persisted receipt count unchanged.

findings.location: permission filter lines 148-155 and denied_count at line 215; repository schema retrieval_receipts at repository.py:200-217
findings.problem: A denied or empty retrieval leaves nothing durable behind. denied_count exists only on the in-memory EvidenceBundle; no row is written anywhere. Probe P2: a non-owner querying a private item produced denied_count=1 and 0 persisted rows, and the golden harness's negative-unauthorized control behaves identically. The ledger can answer 'what evidence was released?' but cannot answer 'did anyone attempt to reach evidence they were not entitled to?' -- and repeated denied attempts are exactly what an auditor of a governed retrieval platform looks for. This is consistent with the locked contract (RetrievalReceipt is defined per released evidence item, docs/sprint-1-contracts.md:236-259) and acknowledged in docs/golden-baseline.md:73-79, so it is a scope gap rather than a contract violation, but the gap sits in the audit story the product sells.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a query-level access record -- query, principal, project, retrieval timestamp, returned count, denied count -- written on every governed call including the empty and denied cases. This pairs naturally with the deferred permission_basis field (docs/sprint-1-contracts.md:386-390) and should land with the authorization layer that can populate the basis honestly.

findings.problem: MetadataFilters.projects widens the query scope and the only check is that it contains request.project. No layer verifies that the principal is entitled to the added projects. Reproduced (probe P6b): a request with project='default' and filters.projects=('default','restricted') returned evidence from the restricted project. The guard that does exist works -- probe P6c confirmed a filter set omitting the request project is rejected, so the scope cannot be silently swapped, only widened. In the delivered single-user model this is bounded, because every widened candidate must still pass SingleUserPermissionEvaluator.is_permitted, so the widening principal can only reach items it already owns or was granted; it is a tenancy weakness, not a present authorization bypass. It becomes a real hole the moment a multi-project, multi-principal evaluator lands, because docs/sprint-1-contracts.md:326-344 designates the project as the tenancy boundary for customer deployments.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve Open Question 1 (docs/sprint-1-contracts.md:382-385) before a second principal exists: either restrict v1 to exactly one project per request, or require the PermissionEvaluator to authorize each project in effective_projects and record the granted set on the EvidenceBundle so an auditor can see which scopes were entitled.

findings.problem: 'Latest-state projection plus append-only sync journal' is a locked decision in context.md, and the delivered code honors it -- only _append_journal writes the table and only via INSERT (repository.py:519-536). But nothing at the schema level enforces it. Probe P7c: an ordinary sqlite3 connection to the same database ran UPDATE synchronization_journal SET change_type='purged' followed by DELETE FROM synchronization_journal, taking the table from 2 rows to 0 with no error. Every other structural invariant in this schema is enforced in the DDL (CHECK (tombstone IN (0,1)) at repository.py:122, foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE, uniqueness constraints), which makes the journal -- the one table whose whole purpose is to be an immutable record -- the only unguarded one.
findings.proposed_fix: Add BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers on synchronization_journal that RAISE(ABORT, 'synchronization_journal is append-only'), matching the enforcement level the rest of the schema already uses, and add a test asserting that a direct DELETE against the table fails.

findings.location: requires-python = ">=3.10" at line 10 and the 'Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10' classifier at line 19
findings.problem: src/lee_kb/main.py:20 and src/lee_kb/connectors/local_files.py:62 both import tomllib, which is standard library only from Python 3.11. On Python 3.10 the package installs cleanly against the declared floor and then fails at import with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomllib' -- on the CLI entry point and on the only connector, i.e. on every code path. context.md names ~/.config/lee-kb/config.toml a public contract and expects client deployments to depend on this package, so an incorrect declared floor is not cosmetic. Verified by inspection of both import sites and the pyproject metadata; the CI environment is Python 3.12, so nothing in the test suite exercises the declared floor.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise requires-python to >=3.11 and drop the 3.10 classifier. That is consistent with the stdlib-only rule; the alternative, a tomli fallback guarded on the version, would add a runtime dependency and needs approval.

findings.problem: docs/golden-baseline.md:25-57 publishes a per-question rank table, an 85.0% hit-at-1 figure, and an MRR of 0.925. The harness asserts only that the expected source label and evidence token appear somewhere in the governed top-10 (lines 155-165); no assertion computes hit-at-1 or MRR, and no assertion checks any rank. I recomputed the metrics independently and they match the document exactly, so the document is accurate today -- but nothing keeps it accurate. A ranking or chunking change would leave the harness green while the published baseline silently drifts, and that baseline is the stated bar for adopting semantic retrieval.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the harness compute hit-at-1, hit-at-10, and MRR from the governed bundles and assert them against values pinned in the test or in corpus.toml, so the documented baseline and the measured one cannot diverge without a test failure.

findings.problem: The CLI recovers receipt identifiers by reading every receipt in the database and taking the last len(bundle.evidence) rows, then zipping them positionally with the evidence. retrieve() discards the identifiers record_receipt() already returns (governance.py:197), so the CLI re-derives them from an ordering assumption documented in a comment. This is correct for today's single-process CLI and wrong for any concurrent writer -- the Phase-2 MCP server named in context.md, serving two requests at once, would print receipt identifiers belonging to another principal's retrieval next to this one's evidence, which is exactly the mislabeling the receipt ledger exists to prevent.
findings.proposed_fix: Have governance.retrieve() return the persisted receipt identifiers (a parallel tuple, or a chunk_id -> receipt_id mapping on the bundle) and delete the tail heuristic from the CLI.

findings.problem: self._clock is assigned but never read. It became dead when the S1-R-01 fix removed the evidence-producing path that used it, leaving LexicalRetriever a pure candidate provider. governance.py:144 still constructs the retriever with clock=lambda: retrieval_timestamp, so the call site reads as though the retriever participates in timestamping when it does not. Ruff does not flag it because it is an attribute assignment rather than an unused local.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the clock parameter from LexicalRetriever.__init__ and drop the argument at the governance.py:144 call site.

findings.problem: Include and exclude matching uses fnmatchcase against the root-relative POSIX path, where * crosses directory separators. I confirmed by probe that include = ["*.md"] discovers sub/deep.md as well as top.md, which is not what a user writing a top-level pattern expects, and the documented exclude = [".git/**"] (main.py:63, local_files.py:19) works only because ** degenerates to * under fnmatch rather than because recursive globbing is implemented. Default-deny still holds and over-inclusion is confined to formats registered in FORMAT_HANDLERS, so the impact is configuration surprise rather than exposure -- but across 15 real source roots, surprise about which files get ingested is worth eliminating before the corpus import.
findings.proposed_fix: Either document the fnmatch semantics explicitly in the module docstring and the starter config in main.py, or switch to recursive-glob semantics (PurePath.full_match, or handle ** distinctly from *) so patterns behave the way the documented examples imply.

findings.location: whole file -- no test case exercises the _resolve() containment guard at connectors/local_files.py:438-442
findings.problem: _resolve() rejects a source_object_id whose resolved path leaves its root, which is the connector's containment guarantee. I confirmed it fires for an out-of-root symlink target (the S1-R-10 reproduction raised ConnectorReadError 'source_object_id escapes its root'). No test covers it: the five connector tests cover initial sync, no-op resync, change detection, deletion/tombstoning, and the include/exclude/format registry, none of them containment. The guard could be weakened or removed by a future change -- including the S1-R-10 fix, which touches exactly this code path -- without any test failing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tests asserting ConnectorReadError for relative-path traversal out of the root and for an out-of-root symlink target, landing them together with the S1-R-10 fix so the two changes to this guard are pinned against each other.

correctness_and_failure_handling.justification: Change detection, cursors, and persistence are genuinely idempotent: sync_item journals only real hash changes (repository.py:302-323), an identical resync writes no journal row (probe P8), and the cursor advances inside the same transaction as the write (repository.py:324-327), so it cannot run ahead of the projection -- pinned by tests/test_repository.py:144. The failure handling gap is in the ingestion driver, not the repository: one unfetchable object ends the whole pass and leaves a half-synchronized projection (S1-R-10). The CLI's receipt-identifier reconstruction rests on an ordering assumption that holds today and breaks under concurrency (S1-R-14). The declared Python floor does not match the code's actual requirement (S1-R-18).

governance_and_security.justification: Authorization is fail-closed, precedes evidence assembly, and is now the only public evidence path -- the prior High finding S1-R-01 is fixed and regression-guarded, confirmed by an independent package-wide sweep. Retrieval grants no execution authority: retrieve() returns data only, and a scan of src/lee_kb found no exec, subprocess, or network call. The connector's path-containment guard works but is untested (S1-R-17). The remaining governance findings concern the audit record rather than access control: a refused retrieval over-records (S1-R-02), a denied one records nothing (S1-R-12), project widening is not entitlement-checked (S1-R-05), and the append-only journal has no schema-level guard (S1-R-06).

retrieval_quality.justification: Providers are replaceable as designed: PermissionEvaluator and Repository are ABCs, LexicalRetriever is a candidate provider behind governance.retrieve(), and RetrieverRank plus fused_rank are carried from day one so rank fusion can land without a schema change. Evidence bundles are cited position for position, ordered by strictly ascending fused_rank, and carry all three timestamps. The dominant quality defect is the matcher itself: AND-of-all-tokens makes recall collapse on any paraphrase and makes the recorded baseline unrepresentative of the workload it will be compared on (S1-R-11). Supporting findings: dead clock plumbing left behind by the S1-R-01 fix (S1-R-15) and surprising include/exclude glob semantics that decide what ever reaches the index (S1-R-16).

tests_and_documentation.justification: Coverage of the required scenarios is real: happy path, empty input (tests/test_retrieval.py:159), repeated sync (tests/test_repository.py:66, tests/test_local_connector.py:142), changed source (tests/test_local_connector.py:162), deleted source and tombstoning (tests/test_local_connector.py:201), denied evidence (tests/test_governance.py:106, :115), missing principal (tests/test_governance.py:91), receipts including the empty case (tests/test_governance.py:138), and CLI failure paths (tests/test_cli.py:91, :137, :147). README, context.md, docs/sprint-1-contracts.md, and docs/golden-baseline.md describe delivered behavior and label the office-format and curated-benchmark deferrals honestly; the baseline document reproduces exactly. The gaps are unasserted published metrics (S1-R-13) and an untested containment guard (S1-R-17).

scope_and_dependencies.justification: The delivered slice matches the Sprint 1 scope in context.md with no drift: stdlib only (an AST scan of src/lee_kb against sys.stdlib_module_names found no third-party runtime import), no enterprise infrastructure, no LLM synthesis, CLI as the only surface, lexical before semantic. The two deferrals are declared rather than silent -- office formats stay in the DocumentType enum with a FORMAT_HANDLERS registry that accepts them without redesign, and the golden corpus is labelled a harness proof in both the document and a harness assertion. No documentation claims behavior the code lacks. The only scope-adjacent defect is packaging metadata that promises a Python version the code cannot run on (S1-R-18).

gate.policy: Critical or High findings fail the gate.
gate.note: The two High findings were reproduced end to end against the delivered code in this attempt and are recorded at the severity their impact warrants: a permanent, non-rolled-back abort of the corpus import that blocks the top-ranked next action, and a matcher that returns nothing for normally phrased questions whose answers are indexed. Both are specific and fixable; neither is in the governance core, which passed every invariant check.
